# Bhallātiyajātaka (Ja 504)

**ID:** Ja 504  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Bhallātiyajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul14.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul14.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhallātiyajātaka* (Ja 504) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. The contemporary frame narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana and centers on a dispute between King Pasenadi of Kosala and Queen Mallikā [Fausböll 1887; Galasek 2016]. Following a domestic quarrel regarding conjugal rights, the angry king refused to speak to her, attributing her behavior to foolish pride in the royal luxuries provided to her [Galasek 2016]. When the Buddha arrives for alms, he enquires after Mallikā's absence and reconciles the estranged couple by recounting a story of the past (*atītavatthu*) [Fausböll 1887; Galasek 2016]. In that previous life, the royal couple had lived as fairies (*kinnaras*) who spent a single night separated from each other and subsequently mourned that loss for seven hundred years [Galasek 2016; Rhys Davids 1890]. At the conclusion of the tale, the Buddha reveals the rebirths: the female fairy was Queen Mallikā, while King Bhallātiya was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1887].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: Mil 7.6.9 Sappaṅgapañha

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1887] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 4 (1887) — Supplies the edition text for the opening framing of the dispute between the king and queen and the closing identification of the Bodhisatta as King Bhallātiya.
- [Fausböll 1897] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 7 (1897) — Notes the parallel prose and verse opening formula and the alternative stūpa inscription title Kinnara-jātaka.
- [Galasek 2016] Bruno Galasek, On Presenting Characters and Representation of Persons… Characters in Narrative Suttas of the Majjhima Nikaya (2016) — Details the narrative context of the reconciliation between Pasenadi and Mallikā and their former lives as a couple.
- [Rhys Davids 1890] T. W. Rhys Davids, The Questions of King Milinda (1890) — Documents the quotation of the fairy birds' verses from the Bhallātiyajātaka in the Milindapañha.
